title: First Case of Teeth Growing Out of an Eye Socket - Nautilus
gist: A 16-year-old boy in India had a fully formed canine tooth removed from his left eye socket, an extremely unusual case of ectopic teeth, which more commonly occur in the maxillary sinus.

insights.claim: A 16-year-old boy in India had a fully formed canine tooth removed from his eye socket after a month of painless swelling, a very unusual ectopic tooth case.
insights.speaker: Saroash Shahid
insights.so_what: Rare clinical case with no market impact.

insights.claim: Ectopic teeth most often occur in the maxillary sinus but have also been found in the nasal cavity, palate, chin, jaw joint and eye socket.
insights.speaker: Saroash Shahid
insights.so_what: Clinical awareness of atypical tooth locations.
insights.locator: Ectopic teeth are most often found

insights.claim: A review of 61 published cases found ectopic teeth can go unnoticed for years or cause pain, swelling, headaches or difficulty opening the mouth.
insights.speaker: Saroash Shahid
insights.so_what: Symptoms are nonspecific, so diagnosis can be delayed.
